comparison: Perfect agreement on anticancer activity claims (C11, C83-C85). Both evaluations find the in vitro functional assays (flow cytometry, Western blot, clonogenic assay) robust and convincing with clear dose-response relationships. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on in vivo efficacy claims (C12, C86-C90). Both evaluations affirm the xenograft data demonstrates significant antitumor activity with appropriate statistical analysis. Both rate as SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes the mechanistic inference could benefit from additional validation.

Strong agreement on trastuzumab resistance claims (C13, C94-C99). Both evaluations treat this as a key strength and major contribution of the work. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval suggests longer-term resistance studies would strengthen conclusions, while peer reviewers emphasize this as a particularly robust finding.

Agreement on synthesis and characterization claims (C4, C116-C124). Both evaluations affirm the synthetic methods, yields, and spectroscopic evidence are appropriate and robust. Peer review also includes initial screening data (C5, C54-C62) in same evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on SEAP screening assay claims (C5, C54-C62, C127-C129). OpenEval evaluates screening methodology separately and finds it well-established with sound experimental design. Peer review groups this with synthesis as part of overall robust approach. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on compound selection process (C6, C63-C66). OpenEval emphasizes the logical selection validated by multiple orthogonal assays. Peer review includes this as part of the overall synthesis and screening evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on fluorescence polarization binding data (C69-C75). OpenEval highlights rigorous biophysical characterization with proper quantitative analysis. Peer review groups this with cellular PPI disruption data as compelling evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on cellular PPI disruption claims (C8-C9, C76-C80). OpenEval emphasizes multiple orthogonal cellular assays with appropriate controls. Peer review treats this as part of compelling mechanistic evidence for PPI inhibition. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on mechanistic chain from PPI inhibition to downstream effects (C10, C81-C82). OpenEval finds the mechanistic pathway well-documented with appropriate assays. Peer review accepts these as logical consequences of HER2 inhibition. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on overall conclusions and therapeutic potential (C14-C15, C110-C115). Both evaluations affirm the work represents a promising therapeutic strategy. OpenEval notes claims about 'novel alternative' are somewhat speculative requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers emphasize the evidence is convincing. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluation of SAR analysis (C67-C68, C113). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting computational SAR lacks direct experimental validation and is based on assumptions. Peer review implicitly accepts this as SUPPORTED without explicit discussion, treating it as reasonable inference from screening data.

Agreement on background and context claims (C1-C36). OpenEval confirms these are well-established facts properly cited from literature. Peer review implicitly accepts background context without challenge. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on strategic rationale and chemical scaffold selection (C37-C53, C104-C109). OpenEval finds the choice well-justified by literature precedent. Peer review accepts the study design and scaffold rationale without critique. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on clinical context claims (C91-C93, C100-C103). OpenEval confirms these are properly supported by citations to clinical guidelines. Peer review implicitly accepts this context as appropriate and well-established. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on cell culture methodology (C125-C126). OpenEval notes this as standard routine methodology. Peer review does not raise concerns about methods, treating them as appropriate. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on quantitative binding affinity claim (C111). OpenEval confirms this directly restates FP assay results with appropriate quantification. Peer review includes this in overall therapeutic potential evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Peer review evaluates experimental methods including SEAP assay and resistance model generation (C127-C130) as robust. OpenEval addresses these claims within other results (R2 for SEAP, R10 for resistance model) rather than as a separate methodological evaluation.
